messages.subject: First-order autoregressive (AR1) model for spatiotemporal data
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to develop an MCMC model that involves fitting an AR1 model to a timeseries of data for each of N grid cells. Here is what I have so far (apologies if it is way off base):

library(nimble)

source('dlik.R') # contents of this file are below


N = 40 # grid cells

m = 65 # time steps (years) in timeseries

truth_residuals = matrix(rnorm(N*m,sd=1),N,m) # sample data to fit AR1 parameters to


sample_rho                       = matrix(rnorm(N*10000,sd=1),N,10000)

sample_rho[sample_rho >= 0.999]  = 0.999

sample_rho[sample_rho <= -0.999] = -0.999


sample_sigma                       = matrix(rnorm(N*10000,sd=1),N,10000)

sample_sigma[sample_sigma <= 0.01] = 0.01


Rcode <- nimbleCode({

  # likelihood ==============

  for(i in 1:N) Y[i,1:m] ~ dar1(sigma=sigma0[i],rho=rho0[i])

  # process =================

  for (i in 1:N) sigma0[i] ~ dunif(0.01,max(sigma.all))

  for (i in 1:N) rho0[i] ~ dunif(-0.999,0.999)

})


# Set up model

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(

  code = Rcode,

  constants = list(N = N, m = m),                                                 # Specify constants (fixed, non-data quantities)

  inits = list(sigma0=apply(sample_sigma,1,mean),rho0=apply(sample_rho,1,mean)),  # initial values for sigma and rho

  data = list( Y = truth_residuals)

)


comp <- compileNimble(Rmodel,showCompilerOutput = TRUE)                    # Compile the model

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)                                              # Configure the model

conf$printSamplers()

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)                                                   # Build the MCMC

Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel,showCompilerOutput = TRUE)  # Compile the MCMC in C++

samples <- runMCMC(Cmcmc,niter=1e5,nchains=1)


# dlik.R

# User-defined nimbleFunction for the AR1 distribution

dar1 <- nimbleFunction(

  run = function( x = double(1), sigma = double(0), rho = double(0),

                  log = integer(0, default = 0) ) {


    returnType(double(0))


    m <- length(x)

    w <- x[2:m] - rho*x[1:(m-1)]      # whitened residuals

    sigma.proc <- sigma/sqrt(1-rho^2) # stationary process variance sigma.proc^2

    logdens <- dnorm(x[1],sd=sigma.proc,log=TRUE) + sum(dnorm(w,sd=sigma,log=TRUE))


    if( log ){ return( logdens ) }

    else{ return( exp( logdens ) ) }

})


rar1 <- nimbleFunction(

  run = function(n = integer(0, default = 1),

                 sigma = double(0), rho = double(0) ) {

    returnType(double(0))

    return(1)

})


registerDistributions( list(dar1 = list(

  BUGSdist = "dar1(sigma, rho)",

  types = c("sigma = double(0)", "rho = double(0)")

)))


I'm getting the error "Dimension of distribution argument(s) 'value' does not match required dimension(s) for the distribution 'dar1'. Necessary dimension(s) are 0." More generally I'm pretty sure I'm treating the spatiotemporal nature of the data incorrectly and would appreciate some guidance on the matter.

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: First-order autoregressive (AR1) model for spatiotemporal data
parts:
Hi Alex,

Regarding the error message, that is referring to the fact that 'x' should be a vector not a scalar, so you need `x = double(1)` when defining `dar1`. 
We should clarify that error message - I've made a note for us to do that.

Also, you'll need  `Y[i,1:m]` in your model code.
And as a side note, you don't need `rar1` or `registerDistributions`, though it's ok to have them. As you have it ,`rar1` is not consistent with `dar1` as it returns a scalar, but it's just a placeholder, so it's ok.

Apart from that it should work from a mechanical perspective. Perhaps others will comment on your modeling question - it's a broad question and there are lots of things one can do with spatio-temporal data like this - allowing for spatial structure in 'y' or in 'sigma' or in 'rho'.

-Chris

messages.subject: Re: First-order autoregressive (AR1) model for spatiotemporal data
parts:
I found this thread because I am (was) getting the exact same message, and it looks to me like the error message is incorrect.  Alex already has `x` specified as a vector in the `dar1` distribution, and does have `Y[i,1:m]` in the model code.  And  I also do have `x = double(1)` specified in my custom distribution, and I do specify a vector value on the left-hand side of the tilde in the model code.

When I ran Alex's code

```

Rcode <- nimbleCode({
  # likelihood ==============
  for(i in 1:N) Y[i,1:m] ~ dar1(sigma=sigma0[i],rho=rho0[i])
  # process =================
  for (i in 1:N) sigma0[i] ~ dunif(0.01,max(sigma.all))
  for (i in 1:N) rho0[i] ~ dunif(-0.999,0.999)
})

```
it generated the Dimension error as described. 

But when I skipped the  `registerDistributions` bit, and then ran the `Rmodel <- nimbleModel(` piece, it did NOT generate the error, but generated a message that `NIMBLE has registered dar1 as a distribution based on its use in BUGS code.` There were other errors upon compilation, and the compilation failed. I won't comment on the model itself, but I am really curious why running  `registerDistributions` generates and error message that seems incorrect. As Chris points out, it seems like `registerDistributions` is not necessary, but it seems to cause a problem. Am I missing something?

As an aside, when I tried skipping  `registerDistributions` for my case, I was able to build the model without generating the error.  Also, I'll note that when I tried a version of this distribution where x was specified as scalar, then `registerDistributions` did not seem to be a problem.

Thanks,
Glenn

messages.subject: Re: First-order autoregressive (AR1) model for spatiotemporal data
parts:
A couple additional comments here:

1) The error when using `registerDistributions` is because the `types` argument doesn't specify "value = double(1)". By default it will treat the density value as being scalar if it's not specified. `registerDistributions` does not mix and match `types` information that can be gleaned from the actual 'd' function with what is provided as input to `registerDistributions`. 

2) The model code has `max(sigma.all)`, which won't compile because `sigma.all` is a scalar. (As a side note, `sigma.all` is never specified anywhere but that is just a matter of providing values to the model and wouldn't cause a compilation error.)  It looks like we need to do a better job of error-trapping (or allowing) code where `max` or `min` is applied to a scalar -- I'm filing an issue for us to take a look at that.

I think that addresses the various issues raised in this thread, but let me know if there are further questions/problems.

-chris

I'm trying to develop an MCMC model that involves fitting an AR1 model to a timeseries of data for each of N grid cells. Here is what I have so far (apologies if it is way off base):

library(nimble)

source('dlik.R') # contents of this file are below


N = 40 # grid cells

m = 65 # time steps (years) in timeseries

truth_residuals = matrix(rnorm(N*m,sd=1),N,m) # sample data to fit AR1 parameters to


sample_rho                       = matrix(rnorm(N*10000,sd=1),N,10000)

sample_rho[sample_rho >= 0.999]  = 0.999

sample_rho[sample_rho <= -0.999] = -0.999


sample_sigma                       = matrix(rnorm(N*10000,sd=1),N,10000)

sample_sigma[sample_sigma <= 0.01] = 0.01


Rcode <- nimbleCode({

  # likelihood ==============

  for(i in 1:N) Y[i,1:m] ~ dar1(sigma=sigma0[i],rho=rho0[i])

  # process =================

  for (i in 1:N) sigma0[i] ~ dunif(0.01,max(sigma.all))

  for (i in 1:N) rho0[i] ~ dunif(-0.999,0.999)

})


# Set up model

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(

  code = Rcode,

  constants = list(N = N, m = m),                                                 # Specify constants (fixed, non-data quantities)

  inits = list(sigma0=apply(sample_sigma,1,mean),rho0=apply(sample_rho,1,mean)),  # initial values for sigma and rho

  data = list( Y = truth_residuals)

)


comp <- compileNimble(Rmodel,showCompilerOutput = TRUE)                    # Compile the model

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)                                              # Configure the model

conf$printSamplers()

Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)                                                   # Build the MCMC

Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel,showCompilerOutput = TRUE)  # Compile the MCMC in C++

samples <- runMCMC(Cmcmc,niter=1e5,nchains=1)


# dlik.R

# User-defined nimbleFunction for the AR1 distribution

dar1 <- nimbleFunction(

  run = function( x = double(1), sigma = double(0), rho = double(0),

                  log = integer(0, default = 0) ) {


    returnType(double(0))


    m <- length(x)

    w <- x[2:m] - rho*x[1:(m-1)]      # whitened residuals

    sigma.proc <- sigma/sqrt(1-rho^2) # stationary process variance sigma.proc^2

    logdens <- dnorm(x[1],sd=sigma.proc,log=TRUE) + sum(dnorm(w,sd=sigma,log=TRUE))


    if( log ){ return( logdens ) }

    else{ return( exp( logdens ) ) }

})


rar1 <- nimbleFunction(

  run = function(n = integer(0, default = 1),

                 sigma = double(0), rho = double(0) ) {

    returnType(double(0))

    return(1)

})


registerDistributions( list(dar1 = list(

  BUGSdist = "dar1(sigma, rho)",

  types = c("sigma = double(0)", "rho = double(0)")

)))


I'm getting the error "Dimension of distribution argument(s) 'value' does not match required dimension(s) for the distribution 'dar1'. Necessary dimension(s) are 0." More generally I'm pretty sure I'm treating the spatiotemporal nature of the data incorrectly and would appreciate some guidance on the matter.

On Wednesday, January 25, 2023 at 11:13:39 AM UTC-6 Christopher Paciorek wrote:
A couple additional comments here:

1) The error when using `registerDistributions` is because the `types` argument doesn't specify "value = double(1)". By default it will treat the density value as being scalar if it's not specified. `registerDistributions` does not mix and match `types` information that can be gleaned from the actual 'd' function with what is provided as input to `registerDistributions`. 

2) The model code has `max(sigma.all)`, which won't compile because `sigma.all` is a scalar. (As a side note, `sigma.all` is never specified anywhere but that is just a matter of providing values to the model and wouldn't cause a compilation error.)  It looks like we need to do a better job of error-trapping (or allowing) code where `max` or `min` is applied to a scalar -- I'm filing an issue for us to take a look at that.

I think that addresses the various issues raised in this thread, but let me know if there are further questions/problems.

-chris

On Mon, Jan 23, 2023 at 6:04 PM gesta...@gmail.com <gesta...@gmail.com> wrote:
I found this thread because I am (was) getting the exact same message, and it looks to me like the error message is incorrect.  Alex already has `x` specified as a vector in the `dar1` distribution, and does have `Y[i,1:m]` in the model code.  And  I also do have `x = double(1)` specified in my custom distribution, and I do specify a vector value on the left-hand side of the tilde in the model code.

When I ran Alex's code

```
Rcode <- nimbleCode({
  # likelihood ==============
  for(i in 1:N) Y[i,1:m] ~ dar1(sigma=sigma0[i],rho=rho0[i])
  # process =================
  for (i in 1:N) sigma0[i] ~ dunif(0.01,max(sigma.all))
  for (i in 1:N) rho0[i] ~ dunif(-0.999,0.999)
})
```
it generated the Dimension error as described. 

But when I skipped the  `registerDistributions` bit, and then ran the `Rmodel <- nimbleModel(` piece, it did NOT generate the error, but generated a message that `NIMBLE has registered dar1 as a distribution based on its use in BUGS code.` There were other errors upon compilation, and the compilation failed. I won't comment on the model itself, but I am really curious why running  `registerDistributions` generates and error message that seems incorrect. As Chris points out, it seems like `registerDistributions` is not necessary, but it seems to cause a problem. Am I missing something?

As an aside, when I tried skipping  `registerDistributions` for my case, I was able to build the model without generating the error.  Also, I'll note that when I tried a version of this distribution where x was specified as scalar, then `registerDistributions` did not seem to be a problem.

Thanks,
Glenn
On Saturday, January 21, 2023 at 11:29:34 AM UTC-6 Christopher Paciorek wrote:
Hi Alex,

Regarding the error message, that is referring to the fact that 'x' should be a vector not a scalar, so you need `x = double(1)` when defining `dar1`. 
We should clarify that error message - I've made a note for us to do that.

Also, you'll need  `Y[i,1:m]` in your model code.
And as a side note, you don't need `rar1` or `registerDistributions`, though it's ok to have them. As you have it ,`rar1` is not consistent with `dar1` as it returns a scalar, but it's just a placeholder, so it's ok.

Apart from that it should work from a mechanical perspective. Perhaps others will comment on your modeling question - it's a broad question and there are lots of things one can do with spatio-temporal data like this - allowing for spatial structure in 'y' or in 'sigma' or in 'rho'.

-Chris
